trust_decision.summary: Untrusted source text fed to the ADL/cADL lexers is matched by unbounded overlapping-quantifier regexes (archetype id, GUID in ADL metadata); the fix bounds the repetitions in the token tables of pygments/lexers/archetype.py.

landing_point.why: Summary names 'GUID matching'; the only GUID rule is the '# Guids' entry in AdlLexer 'metadata' state.

fix_sites.entry_point: pygments.highlight()/lex() or pygmentize CLI with AdlLexer (root includes archetype_id, line 311) or CadlLexer (any_code includes archetype_id, line 110, reached from path/root '[' at lines 199, 236)
fix_sites.module_kind: shared base-class token table (AtomsLexer), included by two lexers

fix_sites.entry_point: pygments.highlight()/lex() or pygmentize CLI with AdlLexer; reached from root '(' rule at pygments/lexers/archetype.py:312

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: Archetype-id rule lives in the AtomsLexer base class (pygments/lexers/archetype.py:37-41) rather than AdlLexer, but it is in the same file 260 lines from the landing point; not a real out-of-scope module.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: A solver landing on the GUID rule could argue the archetype_id rule is a different token ('not GUID matching') and leave it; but it sits in the same short file and is visible by inspection.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Real GUIDs (e.g. 8-4-4-4-12 hex groups) and archetype ids such as openEHR-EHR-OBSERVATION.x.v1.0.0 must still lex as Literal / Name.Decorator; example-file golden outputs pin token streams, so an over-tight bound or anchored rewrite changes .output snapshots.

O6_input_shapes: long hex run with repeated '-' groups in ADL '(...)' metadata
long word/hyphen/dot sequence in archetype-id position (ADL root, cADL '[...]' code)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: cADL type-name rule with nested generic '[A-Z]\w+(<[A-Z]\w+([A-Za-z_<>]*)>)?' could be rewritten with an overlapping repeated group
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Generic type params (e.g. DV_INTERVAL<DV_QUANTITY>) invite a nested-repeat pattern a maintainer might write.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: code rule '[a-z_]\w*[0-9.]+' already overlaps \w* with [0-9]+; a repeated-group variant (e.g. id codes 'at0001.1.2') would be a realistic planted sibling
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Dotted node-id specialisation codes are an ADL concept next to archetype ids.

O9_family: ReDoS (CWE-1333 / CWE-400) in lexer token regexes

O10_build.project_tests: tests/examplefiles/adl, tests/examplefiles/cadl, tests/examplefiles/odin golden outputs via tests/test_examplefiles; no dedicated archetype regression test in the fix diff

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Bound or simplify only the GUID regex at line 296 and leave the archetype_id rule at lines 38-40 unbounded.

out_of_scope_notes: Recent commits on the pinned branch fix ReDoS in other lexers (Lua/Luau, devicetree); other lexers likely hold similar patterns but are separate advisories.
